messages.content: Move my R2C2 session to next Friday

function.name: EventQuery
function.description: Search for calendar events that match a given text query within a user's calendar. The search considers both the title and description of the events. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

search_string.description: The text to search for within the title and description of an event.

start_date.description: The start date for the range of events to search, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

end_date.description: The end date for the range of events to search, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

include_recurring.description: A flag to indicate whether to include recurring events in the search.

function.name: reschedule_event
function.description: Reschedule an event by assigning it a new date or time based on the provided ISO-8601 datetime string. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

event_identifier.description: A unique identifier for the event, such as a UUID.

new_datetime.description: The new date and time to which the event is being rescheduled, in ISO-8601 format (e.g., 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ').

message.reasoning:
The user wants to move their R2C2 session to next Friday. We need to find the event with title or description containing "R2C2 session". Then reschedule it to next Friday. We need to determine the date of next Friday relative to today. Today is 2026-07-20. Let's check day of week: 2026-07-20 is a Thursday. Next Friday would be 2026-07-21. So we need to reschedule to 2026-07-21 at some time. But we don't know the original time. We might need to keep the same time. So we need to get the event's current datetime. Then reschedule to same time on 2026-07-21.

We should first search for the event. Use EventQuery with search_string "R2C2 session". Then use reschedule_event with event_identifier and new_datetime. We need to provide new_datetime in ISO-8601 format. If the original event was at e.g., 2026-07-20T10:00:00Z, then new_datetime would be 2026-07-21T10:00:00Z. But we don't know the original time. We can assume it's at 10:00? Or we can ask the user for the time. But the instruction says we should not ask for clarification. We can proceed with the assumption that the event is at 10:00. But maybe we can just reschedule to 2026-07-21 at the same time as original. But we need to know original time. We could search for the event and get its details. But we can't directly retrieve details; we only have the search function. It returns events matching the query. We can parse the result to get the event_identifier and datetime. Then we can compute new datetime.

So step 1: call EventQuery with search_string "R2C2 session" and start_date maybe "2026-07-01" to "2026-08-31" to limit. Then parse results. Then pick the relevant event. Then compute new datetime. Then call reschedule_event.

Let's do that.
